name: Vitamin E
short: Meta-analyses link vitamin E to more haemorrhagic strokes and, at high doses, higher mortality; in the SELECT trial it raised prostate cancer risk in healthy men.
text: In a meta-analysis of nine randomised trials, vitamin E increased the risk of haemorrhagic stroke by 22% and reduced ischaemic stroke by 10%, with no effect on total stroke. A dose-response meta-analysis of 19 trials (135,967 participants) found higher all-cause mortality in trials of high-dosage vitamin E (400 IU/day or more), with increased risk above 150 IU/day; these high-dose trials were often small and in people with chronic diseases. In the SELECT trial of 35,533 relatively healthy men, vitamin E at 400 IU/day significantly increased the risk of prostate cancer (hazard ratio 1.17). No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
